findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done. The prototype gate returns once it finds an accepted decision and matching image tree; it never requires the design skill's init. The only new init instruction is in the story template, which prototype fixes do not use. The named command test also accepts a prototype design and starts a UI fix without running init. The prototype path therefore misses this explicit Done-when requirement.
findings.follow_up: Not done names no owner-approved Done-when item; builder details are guidance.
findings.title: Not done: Every prototype and every story with user-facing parts starts with the design skill's init

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional. This gate recognizes only `yes`, while the existing worker classification in `src/forge/repo.py:594` recognizes both `yes` and `true`. A plan with `User-facing | true` can therefore pass read and approval without a Design line, then start a task Forge treats as user-facing design work. The named test exercises only `yes`.
findings.title: Require a design for User-facing=true plans

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional. This new check validates the design at task start, but a worker can subsequently change `docs/design/<KEY>/` on the task branch while leaving the approved plan unchanged. `src/forge/worker.py:408-419` checks only the plan hash, and `src/forge/story.py:758-786` checks story documents only when their paths changed. A task can therefore close with screens different from the tree the owner approved. The named proof changes screens in the planning checkout before task start; it does not cover a task's changed screens at close.
findings.title: Reject task branches that change the approved design
